mathematical_content: Named BIG Roth theorem for real irrational algebraic integers: infinitely many positive-denominator unreduced integer/natural approximating pairs with error<q^-kappa force kappa<=2. The proof combines monic equation/parameter gap, reduced approximants and balanced degrees, main auxiliary polynomial construction, discrete integer-value lower bound, Taylor upper bound, product budgets and logarithmic contradiction. New mathlib-only conditional equivalence transports the all-exponent pair bound to all LiouvilleWith exponents<=2 and back; the modern integral theorem derives irrationality only when p>2. It is a modern API restatement consuming the original Roth theorem, not an existing mathlib proof.

module_context_overrides.Roth/Main.lean: 287 is the complete integral Roth theorem assembling the preceding polynomial and arithmetic chain. Unlike scalar/helpers it concludes a universal sharp approximation exponent bound; its following algebraic and rational-value results transport that content.
module_context_overrides.Roth/LeanEval.lean: LeanEval uniform epsilon lower bounds are equivalent endpoint formulations for irrational reals;287 supplies the deep integral exponent exclusion and the following reduction extends it algebraically.

Roth.main_lemma.comparison: The main lemma constructs a nonzero controlled auxiliary integer polynomial under explicit degree/scale and approximation premises.287 selects compatible witnesses and derives the global exponent2 contradiction. The construction is essential prior content, not the same theorem.

Roth.roth_log_bound_aux.comparison: 286 assumes scalar budgets and a product>1 to conclude G*kappa<m*(1+4delta).287 proves such premises from algebraic integrality and infinite approximants and supplies an incompatible lower ratio with G positive. The scalar helper alone has no Roth conclusion.

Roth.reduction.comparison: Reduction transfers an algebraic irrational counterexample at exponent>2 to an integral irrational counterexample.287 rules out the integral counterexample using the multivariate proof; transfer and exclusion are distinct.

Roth.exists_degrees.comparison: 278 selects balanced positive natural degrees from finite positive weights/logs.287 uses these in a full Diophantine contradiction, with arithmetic integrality and infinite approximation inputs absent from the rounding theorem.

Roth.one_le_prod_pow_mul_abs_eval.comparison: 279 gives a discrete denominator-cleared nonzero integer evaluation lower bound.287 combines it with existence and analytic upper bounds to rule out too-strong approximations of algebraic integers.

Roth.abs_eval_lt_of_le_index.comparison: 281 gives a finite weighted Taylor upper estimate under degree/index/coefficient and approximation conditions.287 constructs the polynomial and compatible parameters then contradicts a discrete lower bound. Neither estimate alone is the named Roth theorem.

Roth.eventually_div_rpow_lt.comparison: 270 supplies generic exponent-gap absorption at large positive denominators. The modern287 equivalence uses analogous asymptotic loss to absorb existentialC but still consumes the full integral Roth theorem; asymptotics do not establish its arithmetic exclusion.
